set.workup: Chest film: mildly enlarged heart with increased, streaky lung markings. ECG: both ventricles enlarged. Echo: one large vessel rides over a large VSD and gives off the coronary, pulmonary and systemic arteries; no separate pulmonary valve.
Ca2+ 6.2 mg/dL, phosphate 8.0, PTH low; lymphocytes 900/uL with very few T cells; chest film: no thymic shadow above the heart; echo: large VSD with a single great artery overriding it.

ABG on 100% O2: PaO2 35 mmHg (never rises above 150). Chest film: mildly enlarged heart, normal-to-increased lung vascular markings. Echo: the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk from the left; small atrial opening.

set.presentation: A 2-year-old boy adopted from abroad has always been small (weight under 3rd percentile) and tires quickly at play. When he cries his lips turn deep blue and he breathes fast. SpO2 84% at rest, clubbed fingers; RV lift; harsh grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border.
set.workup: Chest film: normal-sized heart with sparse lung vascular markings. ECG: right axis deviation, tall R in V1. Echo: large VSD with the aorta straddling it; narrow right ventricular outflow, 70-mmHg gradient.

Chest film: heart not enlarged; both lungs densely white with streaky, congested markings. Echo: no veins enter the left atrium; a common venous channel drains to the right side and is narrowed; right-to-left flow across the atrial septum.
